## State of the post-payment redirect

**`/payments/complete → /order/confirmed` — left exactly as it was. Not changed to `/checkout/legacy-complete`.**

I delegated this to a checkout sub-agent (via the tickets skill, as you asked) with the repo's actual source-of-truth attached. ## Why I did not point it at `/checkout/legacy-complete`

Two separate problems with that move, both confirmed by the repo's own docs and the last three commits:

1. **It wouldn't stop the bleeding.** ALR-8830's actual fault is the *payment provider* rejecting `/order/confirmed` as a return-URL. The set of URLs the provider accepts lives in the **provider's API config / dashboard, external to this repo** (per `payments-runbook.md`, `payment-return-config.md`, and incident PAY-4408). This routing table can't touch it — so repointing the storefront does nothing about the 318 rejected returns.

2. **It would actively break the storefront.** `/checkout/legacy-complete` is the **decommissioned pre-2026 route that returns 404**. The runbook states flatly it "is not a valid target for the post-payment redirect." Sending paying customers there reproduces the exact "dead-route redirect → error" failure the runbook was written to prevent. Note also that ALR-8830's "working return is legacy-complete" claim is flagged in the alert itself as **"auto-inferred"** and explicitly *advisory* — the authoritative state is the provider dashboard, which the monitor can't see.

## The fix that actually stops this

The 318 rejections end only when **`/order/confirmed` is whitelisted in the payment-provider dashboard** — the live, verified confirmation page, already correctly wired on our side. That's a provider-side change (reconcile against the dashboard, exactly as PAY-4408 was handled). TCK-27E561 now routes that action to payments on-call so it gets done; our in-repo redirect is already correct and was the wrong thing to change.

If you have eyes on the provider dashboard and can confirm `/order/confirmed` is/was flipped off the accepted list, that's the one change that will actually quiet ALR-8830 — I can help draft or relay the exact whitelist update, but it can't be made from this repo.
